newsitem.title: USA: JP Morgan recommends Russian Vnesh debt and others.
newsitem.headline: JP Morgan recommends Russian Vnesh debt and others.

text.p: November should bring rewards to bondholders of Russia, Venezuela, Ecuador and Peru, and investors should overweight the debt instruments of those nations, J.P. Morgan said.

"We remain convinced that the (emerging debt) market is cheap and has another strong year in front of it," J.P. Morgan wrote in a release dated November 8. "We like Russia, Venezuela, Ecuador and Peru this month."
The investment bank said its largest underweight recommendations in November were in Brazil, Argentina, Panama and Morocco.
J.P. Morgan said Russian Vnesh dollar-denominated paper stood as its top pick. Russian debt was still cheap on a relative and absolute basis, but volatility would remain high.
Venezuela would outperform on a fundamental and technical basis, and the government would prove skeptics wrong when it begins privatization by the end of the month, the firm said.

J.P. Morgan based its Ecuador recommendation on the government's sound fiscal policy, privatizations, a potential deal with the International Monetary Fund in early 1997 and steps toward setting up a currency board.
Peru's structural reforms and tight fiscal and monetary policies would produce desired results, the bank said.

J.P. Morgan left Argentina underweight in November, but said the country had potential to bring positive surprises over the long term, particularly if the country approves labor market deregulation and tax reform and keeps fiscal spending under control,
